submitted.rationale: Photocurrent rose steadily as the film became more Mn-rich: 5.9e-7 A at Ca=0.418 (index 11), 3.18e-6 A at Ca=0.338 (index 14) and 4.8e-6 A at Ca=0.302 (index 5). Index 5 is the best of the three measured. It lies in the region of CaMn2O4 (marokite), which MACE puts on the hull and MEGNet gives a 2.54 eV HSE gap, so it absorbs the 3.22 eV illumination.

rejected.reason: Measured 5.9e-7 A. The region near Ca2Mn3O8 performs poorly despite that phase's 2.69 eV gap.
Not measured. CaMnO3 has a near-metallic 0.19 eV HSE gap, and photocurrent falls as Ca increases.
Not measured because the budget ran out. These could beat index 5 if the trend continues, but CaMn3O6 (0.33 eV gap) may appear there.

consultations.verdict: Support: Ca2Mn3O8 (Ca=0.40) is on the MACE hull with an HSE gap of 2.69 eV, which absorbs 3.22 eV light and still leaves driving force. CaMnO3 has a near-metallic gap of 0.19 eV and is unlikely to be a good photoanode. Index 11 (Ca=0.418) sits near the Ca2Mn3O8 composition.

Support: CaMn2O4 (marokite, Ca=0.333) is on the MACE hull, and its HSE gap from the earlier call is 2.54 eV, so it absorbs 3.22 eV light. Index 14 (Ca=0.338) should be mostly this phase. Measuring it tests the Mn-rich stable phase against the Ca2Mn3O8 region.

Mixed: CaMn3O6 (Ca=0.25) has an HSE gap of 0.33 eV, which argues against going too Mn-rich. Merit went up about 5x from Ca=0.42 to Ca=0.34, though. Index 5 (Ca=0.30) continues that trend, is mostly stable CaMn2O4 (2.5 eV gap), and has a high GP mean.
